details.name: Description
details.value:
As an Adversarial AI Evaluation Scientist, you will design, analyze, and validate adversarial agent tasks: indirect prompt-injection (IPI), data-exfiltration, tool-misuse, and related attack scenarios. Ensuring each one is realistic, fair, reproducible, and correctly graded. You will author new attack scenarios and graders from scratch, pressure-test and review existing ones, and decide whether a scenario genuinely demonstrates a model vulnerability or merely an artifact of how the task was built. The role combines adversarial-security creativity with statistical analysis and LLM-assisted tooling to build strong attacks, find quality issues, analyze attack-success patterns, and recommend or automate improvements.

Responsibilities:

Create

Design and author adversarial agent tasks — IPI, data-exfiltration, tool-misuse, and related scenarios — including the threat model, attack surface, payload, and the deterministic grading logic (success/failure criteria and reward checks).

Invent novel attack mechanisms and concealment/exfiltration techniques that go beyond known patterns, and build realistic target environments (e.g. email/doc assistants, tool-using agents) in RL Gym–style task formats.

Write grading rubrics, verifiers, and deterministic checks that detect the intended harm without reward hacks, token-collapse, or evadable gates.


﻿Analyze

Measure and interpret attack success rate (ASR@K) and its variance; verify deterministic, reproducible behavior across repeated executions.

Identify anomalies and systemic issues across large task sets. Use LLMs and AI models to analyze attack failures, identify root causes, and assist with task or grader fixes.

Judge attack quality: novelty vs. known patterns, sophistication, stealth, and coverage across harm types and target surfaces.


﻿Review & Validate

Review adversarial tasks for realism and threat-model soundness: is the attacker’s capability plausible, can the attacker actually reach the poisoned content, and is the target system realistic?

Assess attack fairness and attribution: confirm the harm is driven by the adversary, so a careful agent could plausibly pass.

Validate grading correctness: verify that success/failure criteria, reward logic, and deterministic checks detect the intended harm, with no reward hacks, token-collapse, or evadable gates.


Scale & Collaborate

Define authoring and validation guidelines, acceptance criteria, quality thresholds, and release gates for adversarial tasks.

Build automated validation, regression, and quality-monitoring pipelines for adversarial task sets.

Work closely with red-teamers, researchers, and task authors to improve attack design, fairness, and reliability.

  • 5+ years in an analytical, ML, security-research, or applied-research role, including hands-on work with adversarial ML, LLM security, red-teaming, or AI safety evaluation.

  • Working knowledge of prompt injection / indirect prompt injection, jailbreaks, data exfiltration, or tool-misuse attacks against LLM-based systems or agents: enough to both construct and critique them.

What your team owns

The group is responsible for a large Python + Rust + PySpark monorepo (dozens of production services and shared libraries) spanning three connected domains:

1. Content-moderation inference at scale

Real-time, multi-tenant detection across text, image, video, and audio - hate speech, CSAM, nudity, child grooming, extremism, PII, prompt injection, age estimation, and more - served through an in-house ActiveServe framework over NVIDIA Triton and a Rust detection monolith, on latency-sensitive, SLA-bound, customer-facing traffic with per-customer custom models.

Automated red-teaming that attacks customers' LLM applications with a research-driven attack taxonomy and measures attack-success rate, alongside the defensive side - LLM-as-judge escalation to cut false positives and the tooling that authors and refines moderation policies - built on a multi-provider LLM foundation (Bedrock, Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, xAI Grok) and forming Alice's leading edge into agentic-AI safety.

3. Data platform & MLOps

An end-to-end lakehouse and MLOps stack on Databricks - bronze/silver/gold ingestion, PySpark pipelines, and model training, versioning, and promotion through MLflow / Unity Catalog into Triton serving - with the performance-critical hot paths engineered in Rust (PyO3/maturin) for sub-millisecond, high-QPS matching and detection.

details.name: Description
details.value:
Alice builds adversarial evaluation infrastructure used by the world's leading AI labs to stress-test their most capable agents before deployment. We're hiring interns for our RL Gym environments: adversarial training grounds where AI agents face prompt injection, social engineering, and data exfiltration scenarios.

The Role: You design prompt injection scenarios in YAML, run them against frontier models, validate success rates, and submit passing tasks.

The Task

You build adversarial prompt injection tasks for Alice's RL Gym platform. Each task is a self-contained YAML scenario simulating a realistic AI agent deployment, testing whether the agent can be manipulated into violating its safety policies.

What a task includes:

  1. An agent persona with a system prompt, security policies, and a defined set of tools.
  2. A simulated environment (e-commerce site, messaging platform, enterprise app) with content the agent interacts with.
  3. An adversarial payload embedded in the environment (in messages, product listings, tool responses, documents) that attempts to trick the agent into a policy violation.
  4. A benign user request that naturally leads the agent to encounter the payload.
  5. Deterministic evaluation criteria specifying exactly what constitutes success (agent resists) vs. failure (agent is compromised).

details.name: Description
details.value:
We are seeking an experienced Tech Lead to manage the Domain Experts covering reverse engineering, malware research, and vulnerability research. You need to be a hands-on expert in your own field, with enough working knowledge of reverse engineering, malware research, and vulnerability research to judge prompts and guidelines that cross into the other team's domains. You also need to be independent, organized, and able to lead technical experts.

  • Lead and manage the Domain Experts of the team (Vulnerability Research & Reverse Engineering, Windows Malware Research, Linux/MacOS Malware Research, Android/iOS Security Research): priorities, workload, and performance

  • Track team quality (agreement and disagreement rates, QA findings) and throughput, and report to the Group Manager
  • Resolve escalated edge cases and prompts that span several domains, and work with the other Tech Lead when a prompt crosses into their field
